questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Academic and cultural aspects. The academic level af Vrije Universiteit is very good. And Amsterdam is a beautiful and interesting city to live in.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The VU exchange team is very helpful and you receive plenty of information upon arrival. They are also extremely quick at responding to emails.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received several emails concerning practical matters and student housing beforehand. I also attended a webinar on course selection for exchange students. The exchange team organizes an introduction week, where you also will be informed on many important matters.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Going on exchange will always involve a great amount of dealing with bureaucracy and administrative work. But if you actively search for the information available, it is a lot easier.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Vrije Universiteit offers student housing via the company DUWO. Finding housing in Amsterdam is stressful, but if you sign up via DUWO (which you will be informed on via email from the university) then you don't need to worry. DUWO usually has housing for everyone, as long as you are on time. So make sure to stay updated on the deadlines and be patient.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Student housing offers either a private kitchen or communal kitchen, depending on the type of accommodation you choose.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: If you are a social and open-minded person, it is so much fun living in campus housing. I met some of my best friends on exchange there, and it defined my whole experience abroad. It adds a great social element and it is such an easy way to meet new people.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The conditions of the student housing are not great. But i think you get great value for money, especially since Amsterdam is currently in a housing crisis.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: All the emails very helpful and informative.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: After accepting your mobility from KU, you register at your host institution before a certain date.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Informational emails. I also wrote several emails to the exchange team at Vrije Universiteit and they were helpful and quick to respond.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was able to successfully register for all my classes.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just be on time and look out for the dealines.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Vrije Universiteit offers a diversity of courses with many different learning styles, which i found very interesting.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
The Netherlands is overall recognized for a high academic level. My courses varied a lot in difficulty, some were easy and some were quite challenging. Look out for the course manual, which describes a certain amount of points for each course (100, 200 or 300). Courses with 300 are higher level. 

Passing a course with minimal effort is not always certain at Vrije Universiteit. But if you keep up with your lectures and readings, you will be fine.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
In some of my smaller classes, the style of teaching was very engaging. It included group work, oral presentations, class debates etc. and i honestly found the style of teaching a lot more inspiring and motivating than at UCPH. 

However, most of my exams were multiple choice, which is very different from UCPH. So studying is mostly centered on just memorizing concepts

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Comparative Politics: Democracies and Other Regimes
EU Governance in an International Context
The Governance and Politics of Social Problems
Philosophy and the Ethics of Political Violence: Peace, War and Terrorism
Philosophy CIS-L&SMKDA

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I can highly recommend the course Philosophy and the Ethics of Political Violence: Peace, War and Terrorism, taught by Prof. Dr. Fernando Enns and Dr. Andrés Pacheco Lozano. I genuinely enjoyed this course and i learned a lot. The two professors are very inspiring and engaging teachers.

questions.answer: Signing up for housing via DUWO. Paying for a bike subscription each month (but both costs are worth it)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing was less expensive, as i signed up for a cheaper student housing option via DUWO.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is my impression that the student clubs and associations are mostly for Dutch students, so i did not seek them out.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many i think.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did not get involved.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Enjoy the city's many parks, cafes, museums and markets. Visit the other famous Dutch cities nearby.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, Amsterdam is very similar to Copenhagen.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Maybe not local students, but living in student housing makes it easy to socialize with other international exchange students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing really.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Very nice food markets and flee markets every weekend.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1) enjoy what Amsterdam has to offer 2) live in the student dorms if you want to meet new people and socialize with people from different cultures 3) do not stress too much about school and enjoy your time

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It can seem overwhelming having many courses (5 in one semester) and having exams and mid-terms quite often. But in reality i never felt stressed a single time and everything worked out fine.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting people from many different cultures, making new friends and gaining new perspectives.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Bureaucracy and administration work from my sending institution.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I highly recommend going on exchange to everyone!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
